title: sendKeysVerified re-sends the same narration up to 3x when the idle gate times out: the delivery oracle's precondition (idle pane) is provably violated at exactly that moment
description:
OBSERVED LIVE (ship of PR #298): the same `[cam]` narration line arrived in the orchestrator pane THREE times. Grounding proves this is a send-layer defect, distinct from CAM-361 (which is about the 30s BLOCKING window, not duplication).

MECHANISM (all cited, src/tmux/dispatch.ts):
- :503 `waitForIdlePane` returns timedOut=true when the pane never goes idle within IDLE_WAIT_DEADLINE_MS (30_000, :256).
- :504-509 the ONLY consequence is a stderr warning. No return, no flag, no maxAttempts reduction. Control falls through into the retry loop.
- :512 `for (attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++)` with maxAttempts default 3 (:480). The send at :519 is UNCONDITIONAL inside the loop body.
- :529-539 delivered = (baseline !== null && after !== null && geometryUnchanged(...)) && cursorRowStartsWithPrompt(...). The only break is :537.
- There is NO de-duplication, idempotency key, or already-sent guard anywhere between :512 and :550. `delivered` is set ONLY by a successful verification, never by the act of sending.

RESULT: up to 3 REAL deliveries of the same payload per call. tmux send-keys always succeeds at the transport level, so each retry genuinely lands.

THE CRUX, MEASURED 2026-07-20 on the live orchestrator pane (238x76) while it was BUSY mid-response: `tmux list-panes -F '#{cursor_x},#{cursor_y}'` read `2,72`, and the cursor row content started with the prompt glyph U+276F. That is byte-INDISTINGUISHABLE from an idle empty composer. The oracle's measured basis (dispatch.ts:38-46, :347-354) is explicitly scoped to an IDLE pane; there is no measurement in the source for a pane that is mid-response, spinning, or streaming.

So the logical hole is precise and does not depend on further probing: when the idle gate TIMES OUT, the code KNOWS the oracle's precondition is violated, and it nonetheless consults that oracle and retries on its verdict. The idle gate uses pane CONTENT (isOrchPaneIdle) and correctly detects busy; the delivery oracle uses cursor GEOMETRY and provably cannot.

PROPOSED FIX (direction, not a mandate): when waitForIdlePane reports timedOut, send exactly ONCE and do not enter the verify/retry cycle, emitting the existing 'push-undelivered' observational event (:552-554) instead of a verdict the oracle is not entitled to render. Delivering a best-effort narration line once-unverified is strictly better than delivering it three times.

Sidecar-executed (host.ts:330 -> dispatch.ts), so this needs a coherence rebuild.

NOT to be conflated with CAM-361: that issue covers the 30s SYNCHRONOUS stall of the sidecar outer loop. This one is the duplicate delivery. They share a trigger (busy pane) but have different fixes and different blast radii.
